title: 第二十一章第一刀二十二集网第五章婴宁
lines: 第二十一章第一刀
沈默决定从阿芸的案子开始。
他不知道这个案子会通向哪里，他只知道，一个人死了，死得不明不白，衙门说是自杀，但尸体告诉他不是。他信尸体。尸体不会说谎。

他白天去城南的桥下，看现场。桥是石头的，很旧，栏杆上长着青苔。阿芸就是吊在这座桥的栏杆上。沈默蹲下来，看栏杆上的痕迹。绳子磨过的痕迹还在，很深，说明阿芸吊上去之后，还挣扎过。他站起来，沿着桥走了两遍。桥头连着一条巷子，巷子很窄，两边是高墙，墙上长着草。他蹲下来，看地上的脚印。脚印很多，乱的，分不清是谁的。但他注意到，墙根底下有一片草被踩倒了，草叶上有一点暗红色的东西。他凑近了看，是血。他用手指沾了一点，放在鼻子底下闻。是人血。
他顺着那片被踩倒的草往前看，草一路倒过去，延伸到巷子深处。有人从这里跑过，跑得很急，摔了一跤，手撑在墙根，留下了血。沈默站起来，跟着那片倒伏的草往前走。走了大约五十步，草没了，脚印也没了。前面是一条大路，人来人往，什么痕迹都找不到了。
他站在路口，看着来来往往的人，站了很久。然后他转身，回到义庄。
夜里，他又去看阿芸的尸体。
义庄很静，只有油灯的火苗在跳。他把白布掀开，把油灯挪近了些。尸体的脸已经肿了，发青，但他还是能看清那些痕迹。他把手放在那道手勒的痕迹上，比了比。手指的间距，比他的手宽，比他粗。是一个男人的手。他用尺子量了，记在本子上。
然后他从怀里掏出一把刀。刀很薄，很小，刀刃在油灯下泛着冷光。刀柄是凉的，握在手里很沉。他深吸一口气，刀尖抵住阿芸指甲缝里的淤血，手腕轻轻一抖。皮屑被完整地挑出，落在一张白纸上。他的手很稳，没有抖。他做了十年仵作，看过上千具尸体，从来没有抖过。
他又看她的手腕。手腕上有淤青，是被人攥出来的。攥得很紧，指印清晰。他拿尺子量了，记在本子上。又看她的脚踝，脚踝上有擦伤，是拖拽造成的。她被人从巷子里拖到桥上，脚踝磨破了。
沈默把白布盖好，坐在义庄门口，等着天亮。
他脑子里有一个画面：阿芸从巷子里跑出来，后面有人追。她跑得很急，摔了一跤，手撑在墙根，留下了血。那人追上来，掐住她的脖子。她挣扎，抓破了他的手。那人掐死了她，把她拖到桥上，吊起来，做成自杀的样子。
那个人是谁？沈默不知道。但他知道，那个人手上有一个疤，在虎口。阿芸抓破了他的手，留下了皮屑和血丝。只要找到那个人，比对伤口，就能定罪。
天快亮的时候，他闭上眼睛，眯了一会儿。梦里，他看见一个女人站在桥下，浑身湿透，脸是白的，眼睛是黑的。她看着他，不说话。他站在那里，看着她，看了很久。然后她转身，走了，消失在雾里。
他醒来的时候，天已经亮了。他坐在义庄门口，浑身是汗。他站起来，走到桥下，站在那里，看着桥上的栏杆。栏杆上还有绳子磨过的痕迹，深深的，像一道疤。
沈默开始查阿芸的身份。
他去了城南，问了几户人家。没有人认识阿芸。他又去了城西，问了几天，终于找到一个认识她的人。是个老婆婆，在街边卖豆腐脑。老婆婆说，阿芸是从外地来的，在这里无亲无故，靠给人洗衣裳过活。她住在城西的一条巷子里，租了一间小屋。
沈默去了那条巷子。小屋很破，门没锁，推开进去，里面只有一张床、一张桌子、一把椅子。床上铺着草席，席子上有一件没洗好的衣裳。桌上有一个碗、一双筷子、一盏油灯。沈默翻了翻，没有找到任何能证明她身份的东西。他站在屋里，看着那件没洗好的衣裳。衣裳是男人的，绸缎的，很贵。不是阿芸自己能穿得起的。
他把衣裳叠好，揣进怀里。
他问了邻居。邻居说，阿芸很少和人说话，每天早出晚归，不知道她在哪里洗衣裳。有时候夜里会有人来找她，什么人都有，男人女人，老人年轻人。她从来不让人进屋，站在门口说了几句话，就把人打发走了。
沈默问：“最近有没有人来找她？”
邻居想了想。“有。半个月前，有个男人来找她。穿得很好，骑着一匹马。阿芸不让他进屋，两个人在门口说了很久。后来男人走了，阿芸关上门，哭了一夜。”
“那个男人是谁？”
“不知道。没见过。但听口音，是本地人。”
沈默记下了。他走出巷子，站在路口，看着来来往往的人。他想起阿芸指甲缝里的皮屑，想起她手腕上的淤青，想起她脚踝上的擦伤。他想起那个男人，穿着绸缎衣裳，骑着一匹马，在夜里来找她。
他握紧了拳头。
那天夜里，沈默在义庄整理证据。他把白纸上的皮屑小心地包好，放在一个木盒里。他把量好的尺寸誊在本子上，一笔一画，写得很慢。油灯的火苗跳了一下，他的影子投在墙上，晃了晃。
他忽然觉得有什么不对。他抬起头，看见门口站着一个人。
那人不知何时来的，无声无息。他穿着一件旧袍子，脸色很白，白得不像是活人的颜色。他站在那里，不动，不说话。月光穿过他身后，照在地上，他的影子很淡。
沈默的手停在半空。他看着那个人，那个人看着他。
“你是谁？”沈默的声音很平。
那人没有回答。他走进来，走到沈默面前，低头看着桌上的木盒和本子。他的眼睛很亮，像两颗浸在溪水里的黑石子。
“阿芸的案子，查到了？”那人问。声音很轻，像风吹过水面。
“查到了。”沈默说。“周乡绅。半个月前，他去找阿芸。阿芸不让他进屋，他走了。第二天夜里又来了。这一次，阿芸跑了，从巷子里跑出去，跑到桥上。他追上她，掐死了她，吊在栏杆上。”
那人点了点头。“证据呢？”
“没有。证人不敢作证。周乡绅有钱有势，没人敢得罪他。”
那人沉默了一会儿。“证据的事，我来想办法。你去告。”
沈默看着他。“你怎么想办法？”
那人没有回答。他转身走了。走到门口，停下来，回头看了一眼。月光照在他脸上，他的眼睛很亮。
“沈默，你只管告。别的，交给我。”
他走了。沈默追到门口，街上空荡荡的，一个人也没有。月光照在地上，白花花的，像铺了一层霜。地上的尘土平整如初，连一个脚印都没有。那人像是融进了月光里，不见了。

Chapter 21 The First Sword
Silence decided to start with Ayun's case.
He didn't know where this case would lead. He only knew that a man died in an unknown manner. The Yamen said it was suicide, but the corpse told him it was not. Thaksin corpse. Corpses don't lie.
During the day, he went under the bridge in the south of the city to watch the scene. The bridge is made of stone and is very old, with moss growing on the railings. Ayun is hanging on the railing of this bridge. Shen Mo squatted down and looked at the marks on the railing. The traces of the rope being worn were still very deep, indicating that Ayun struggled after being hung up. He stood up and walked along the bridge twice. There is an alley connected to the end of the bridge. The alley is very narrow, with high walls on both sides and grass growing on the walls. He knelt down and looked at the footprints on the ground. There were so many footprints in such a mess that it was hard to tell who belonged to them. But he noticed that there was a piece of grass that had been trampled down under the wall, and there was something dark red on the grass blades. He looked closer and saw blood. He put a little on his finger and put it under his nose to smell it. It's human blood.
He looked forward along the piece of trampled grass. The grass fell all the way and extended into the depths of the alley. Someone was running by here, running very fast, and fell down. His hand was on the wall, leaving blood. Silence stood up and followed the fallen grass forward. After walking about fifty steps, the grass was gone and the footprints were gone. There is a big road ahead, with people coming and going, but no traces can be found.
He stood at the intersection for a long time, watching the people coming and going. Then he turned around and returned to Yizhuang.
At night, he went to see Ayun's body again.
Yizhuang is very quiet, only the flame of the oil lamp is dancing. He lifted the white cloth and moved the oil lamp closer. The corpse's face was swollen and blue, but he could still see the marks clearly. He put his hand on the mark of the strangulation and gestured. The distance between the fingers is wider than his hand, thicker than him. It's a man's hand. He measured it with a ruler and wrote it down in his notebook.
Then he took out a knife from his pocket. The knife was very thin and small, and the blade glowed coldly under the oil lamp. The handle of the knife is cold and feels heavy in the hand. He took a deep breath, pressed the tip of the knife against the blood between Ayun's fingernails, and flicked his wrist. The skin flakes were picked out completely and fell on a piece of white paper. His hands were steady, not shaking. He has been working as a police officer for ten years and has seen thousands of corpses, but he has never been shaken.
He looked at her wrist again. There were bruises on his wrists, from being pinched. The grip was tight and the fingerprints were clear. He measured it with a ruler and wrote it down in his notebook. Looking at her ankles again, there were scratches on them, caused by dragging. She was dragged from the alley to the bridge and her ankles were bruised.
Shen Mo covered her with a white cloth and sat at the door of Yizhuang, waiting for dawn.
There was a picture in his mind: Ayun ran out of the alley, and someone was chasing her. She ran so fast that she fell and put her hand on the wall, leaving blood. The man caught up and grabbed her neck. She struggled and scratched his hand. The man strangled her to death, dragged her to the bridge, hung her up, and made it look like she was committing suicide.
Who is that person? Silence doesn’t know. But he knew that the man had a scar on his hand, which was in the tiger's mouth. Ayun scratched his hand, leaving skin flakes and bloodshot eyes. As long as you find that person and compare the wounds, you can convict him.
When it was almost dawn, he closed his eyes and squinted for a while. In the dream, he saw a woman standing under the bridge, soaked to the skin, with a white face and black eyes. She looked at him without speaking. He stood there and looked at her for a long time. Then she turned around and walked away, disappearing into the mist.
When he woke up, it was already dawn. He sat at the door of Yizhuang, covered in sweat. He stood up, walked under the bridge, and stood there, looking at the railings on the bridge. There are still marks on the railings where the rope has been worn, deep like a scar.
Silence begins to check Ayun's identity.
He went to the south of the city and asked several families. No one knows Ayun. He went to the west of the city again and asked for a few days, and finally found someone who knew her. She is an old woman selling tofu bread on the street. The old woman said that Ayun came from another place and had no relatives or friends here, so she made a living by washing clothes for others. She lived in an alley in the west of the city and rented a small house.
Silence went to that alley. The hut was very dilapidated, and the door was unlocked. When you pushed it in, there was only a bed, a table, and a chair inside. The bed was covered with a straw mat, and there was an unwashed piece of clothing on the mat. There is a bowl, a pair of chopsticks, and an oil lamp on the table. Shen Sheng rummaged through it, but couldn't find anything that could prove her identity. He stood in the room, looking at the unwashed clothes. The clothes were men's, made of silk and very expensive. It's not something Ayun can afford to wear herself.
He folded the clothes and put them in his arms.
he asked his neighbor. Neighbors said that Ayun seldom talked to people and went out early and came back late every day. They didn't know where she washed her clothes. Sometimes people would come to her at night. They were all kinds of people, men and women, old and young. She never let people in. She stood at the door and said a few words before sending people away.
Shen Mo asked: "Has anyone come to see her recently?"
The neighbor thought for a moment. "Yes. Half a month ago, a man came to see her. He was well dressed and riding a horse. Ayun refused to let him in, and the two of them talked at the door for a long time. Then the man left, and Ayun closed the door and cried all night."
"Who is that man?"
"I don't know. I haven't seen him before. But from the accent, he is a local."
Silence took note. He walked out of the alley and stood at the intersection, watching the people coming and going. He thought of the skin flakes between Ayun's fingernails, the bruises on her wrists, and the scrapes on her ankles. He thought of the man, wearing silk clothes and riding a horse, coming to her at night.
He clenched his fists.
That night, Shen Mo collected evidence in Yizhuang. He carefully wrapped the scraps of skin on the white paper and placed them in a wooden box. He copied the measured dimensions into a notebook, drawing them one stroke at a time, writing very slowly. The flame of the oil lamp jumped, and his shadow was cast on the wall, shaking.
He suddenly felt something was wrong. He raised his head and saw someone standing at the door.
The man didn't know when he came and made no sound. He was wearing an old robe, and his face was very white, too white to look like a living person. He stood there, motionless and silent. The moonlight passed behind him and shone on the ground, making his shadow very faint.
The silent hand stopped in mid-air. He looked at the man, and the man looked at him.
"Who are you?" The silent voice was calm.
The man didn't answer. He walked in, walked to Shen Mo, and looked down at the wooden box and notebook on the table. His eyes were bright, like two black pebbles soaked in the stream.
"Has Ayun's case been investigated?" the man asked. The sound was very soft, like wind blowing across the water.
"Found it." Shen Mo said. "Squire Zhou. Half a month ago, he went to find Ayun. Ayun wouldn't let him enter the house, so he left. He came again the next night. This time, Ayun ran away from the alley and ran to the bridge. He caught up with her, strangled her, and hung her on the railing."
The man nodded. "Where's the evidence?"
"No. Witnesses dare not testify. Squire Zhou is rich and powerful, and no one dares to offend him."
The man was silent for a while. "As for the evidence, I'll figure it out. You go and sue."
Look at him silently. "How do you think of a solution?"
The man didn't answer. He turned and left. Walking to the door, he stopped and looked back. The moonlight shines on his face, and his eyes are bright.
"Silence, just complain. Leave the rest to me."
He's gone. Silence chased to the door, the street was empty, there was no one. The moonlight shines on the ground, which is covered with white flowers, like a layer of frost. The dust on the ground was as smooth as before, without even a single footprint. The figure seemed to melt into the moonlight and disappeared.
